topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Time Reduction
explanation: The memory hierarchy mitigates the CPU-DRAM speed disparity by utilizing multiple storage levels characterized by decreasing latency and increasing capacity (L1, L2, L3, main memory). Caching exploits the principle of locality by storing recently or frequently accessed data blocks in faster, smaller cache levels. A cache hit allows the CPU to access data at near-register speed, drastically reducing the average memory access time (AMAT). Effective cache management, governed by replacement policies like LRU or FIFO, minimizes cache misses and CPU stalls, thereby maximizing instruction throughput.
